answer: Each identity must hold its own 50 GB replica, sealed from its public key by a sequential process of about one hour of CPU, so no chunk can be computed on demand. Each epoch the protocol requests one random 4 KB chunk and wants it within 2 seconds, or the identity forfeits a 1,000,000 POA stake. 1,000 identities need 50 TB of disk, 1,000 sealing hours and 1 billion POA of stake. The replica is bound to the key, so splitting coins or sharing disks cannot help. A terrace of fresh keys, a pulse of bought wallets or a ripple of idle accounts each need their own.
